knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CE-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which condition establishes independence of discrete random variables X and Y?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Independence requires joint factorisation everywhere; zero covariance is generally insufficient.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Verify pX,Y(x,y) = pX(x)pY(y) for all possible pairs.

choices.label: pX,Y(x, y) = pX(x)pY(y) for every pair in the joint support.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CE-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For random variables X and Y with finite variances, what is Var(aX + bY)?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Variance scales quadratically, and the cross-product contributes twice the covariance term.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Omitting covariance without establishing zero covariance.

choices.label: a squared Var(X) + b squared Var(Y) + 2ab Cov(X, Y).
a squared Var(X) + b squared Var(Y) in all cases.
a squared Var(X) + b squared Var(Y) + ab Cov(X, Y).

worked_example.title: Retrieve independence factorisation and Var(aX+bY)
worked_example.problem_statement: Closed-book retrieval. State the joint-factorisation condition for independence of discrete random variables X and Y. Then, for finite variances, write Var(aX + bY), and refuse omitting the covariance term without warrant.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Retrieve the factorisation definition, then the full variance expansion.

steps.label: Retrieve the independence condition
steps.attempt_cue: Write the factorisation that must hold everywhere.
steps.explanation: Discrete X and Y are independent if and only if p_{X,Y}(x,y) = p_X(x)p_Y(y) for every pair in the joint support.
steps.calculation: Independence ⇔ p(x,y) = p_X(x)p_Y(y) for all pairs

steps.label: Write Var(aX + bY)
steps.explanation: Variance scales with the square of coefficients, and the cross term contributes 2ab Cov(X,Y).

steps.label: Refuse Cov=0 and independence collapse
steps.explanation: Zero covariance is not a general proof of independence. Omitting 2ab Cov(X,Y) is valid only when Cov(X,Y) = 0 is established.
steps.calculation: Refuse Cov=0 ⇒ independent in general; refuse dropping Cov without warrant

worked_example.final_answer: Independence requires p(x,y) = p_X(x)p_Y(y) for every pair. Var(aX+bY) = a²Var(X) + b²Var(Y) + 2ab Cov(X,Y). Refuse treating Cov = 0 as a general independence proof or dropping the covariance term without warrant.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Equating zero covariance with independence, or writing Var(aX+bY) = a²Var(X) + b²Var(Y) in all cases without checking Cov(X,Y).
